question: Does evidence of humans from 45,000 years ago contradict the belief that Adam lived 6,000 years ago?
asked: She read an article in a magazine that a painting made by humans has been discovered in a cave that goes back 45,000 years. Does this not clash with our belief that Adam was around 6,000 years ago from our time?
answer:
So this is a question that deals with chronology. It deals with timeframes. And she is asking a question that there seems to be a conflict between the archaeological evidence for the existence of mankind and the notion that we have been on this earth for 6,000 years.

So with regards to the archaeological evidence, it does appear to be pretty conclusive. There are multiple genres of evidences, not just one evidence. There are multiple areas, if you like, of study that demonstrate that our species of mankind, of human beings, our particular species (we're not talking about Cro-Magnon or Neanderthal or Homo erectus or Homo habilis; we're talking about actual us, as Homo sapiens), our species has been around for at least 50, 60,000 years at the very least. This is pretty much definitive now, in terms of so many evidences.

You have only brought one evidence, which is paintings in a cave, and there are paintings in multiple areas. A famous cave in France was covered up and basically left untouched for 25,000 years, and it was discovered only a few years ago because of a certain crevice that opened up. And you find paintings that can be easily carbon-14 dated, and handprints, and there are modern archaeologists that have put their hand next to the original, and it is exactly the same. This is human beings. And you see art; no other species is drawing art other than us. So you see art of an animal, you see recognizable animals that would have been around 45,000 years ago as well.

The Aborigines in Australia: there is evidence that they have been there for around 40,000 years. There's archaeological evidence, bones and whatnot. And the Aborigines are of the most ancient of all races that have been cut off from the mainstream of humanity, and so quite a lot of research has been done on them, their genetic structures and whatnot. And other things also point to mankind having been on this earth for, as I said, at least 40 to 50,000 years, if not more. Some have posited even a few more millennia than this. But the point being, yes, it is pretty definitive.

Now the next thing you mentioned is that Adam existed 6,000 years ago. And this is where we say: where did you get this number from? Because we firmly believe that there cannot be an actual clash between definitive science and explicit and authentic scripture. There cannot be an actual clash between something that is certain and clear-cut from observable science and phenomena, and something that is in the Qur'an or authentic Sunnah that is clear in meaning.

Why? Because the Qur'an is from Allah, and Allah is also our Creator. And so to Allah belongs the creation and the command: *ala lahu al-khalqu wa al-amr*. So the creation is the world around us, and the command is the Qur'an and the speech of Allah. So when both of them come from Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, the one of them created and the other uncreated, then how can there be a conflict between the two? We believe firmly there can never be a definitive conflict. If there is, it is a perceived one in our minds, and we need to work out how to reconcile.

And in this particular case, we say that this 6,000 timeframe that you are coming from, in reality, is not based on any Islamic sources. It is coming from Judeo-Christian sources. We as Muslims do not believe necessarily that Adam existed 6,000 years ago. Rather, this is something that some segments of Judaism, and in particular Orthodox Judaism... And of course they have a calendar, by the way. Like we have the Hijri calendar, and the Christians have the Gregorian calendar, and other civilizations have their calendars, the Jewish people have their calendar. And in their calendar, they date the beginning of their calendar from the time of Adam. That is their mythology.

And according to them... our year is 2021 in the Gregorian, meaning ours, the Western civilization; and in the Jewish civilization, their year is 5781. So we are currently in the year 5781. So according to the Jewish calendar, Adam existed 5,781 years ago. However, that is something that is found in their sources. We do not have to have this particular timeframe.

And in fact, we are not bound by any dates. And therefore, as Muslims, we say that we do not have a theological chronology. We don't have a calendar or a timeframe that we are bound to believe in. And so people are free to believe whatever they want from an Islamic perspective. So if somebody, for whatever reason, wants to believe 6,000, that's their prerogative; nobody's saying that, as a Muslim, Islam tells us to do that. And if somebody says, "Well, science tells us that we've been here for 50,000 years, so we're going to have to extrapolate Adam alayhi salam to be back 50,000 years or whatever," that too is permissible. **The Shari'ah does not have any numbers when it comes to dates.** So alhamdulillah, we thank Allah that there is no actual conflict between the chronology of science in this regard and the chronology of theology, because we do not have this.

In fact, in my other lectures I have mentioned that we actually might have some evidence to indicate that the 6,000 does not make any sense. And of them is a hadith, even though it is very weak (some have said batil), that it is alleged that our Prophet would stop his nasab, or his lineage, when he gets to Adnan. And Adnan is 20 generations before the Prophet, and then he would not go beyond this. And there is a report that he would say that the scholars of lineage are lying or mistaken; they do not know who is before Adnan, because Allah says in the Qur'an... this is Surah Furqan, verse 38. This is a key verse.

Now, the hadith might be from Ibn Abbas. It's not from the Prophet ﷺ. It's ascribed to him in the books, but in reality it has people in the chain that make us say that it's not authentic. In fact, it might be batil or maybe even mawdu'. But it might be from a Tabi'i, or maybe even Ibn Abbas. And the concept that we don't know who is beyond Adnan, this is an authentic concept.

By the way, who is Adnan? Adnan is the father of one of the two main branches of the Arabs. The Arabs were two main branches; we can very simplistically say middle Arabia and South Arabia. And you had Adnan and Qahtan to be these two major players that were roughly in the same timeframe. And the Arabs would consider that the descendants of both Adnan and Qahtan, these are what make all of the Arab tribes. So all of the Arab tribes were divided into Adnani or Qahtani. And our Prophet was an Adnani. And Adnan was of the descendants of Isma'il, and Isma'il was of the descendants of Nuh, and Nuh was of the descendants of Adam.

However, the names of the individuals between Adam and Nuh, and between Nuh and Ibrahim, and between Ibrahim and Adnan, this is something that we do not know. Now, you will find charts in many Muslim households; in many seerah books you will find charts that have names, but we do not know. We do know for certain, pretty much, and the history is pretty clear, up to Adnan, because the Arabs documented their tribes. The Arabs documented the founders. And so: who is Quraysh, and the descendants of Quraysh, and the ancestors of Quraysh all the way to Adnan.

However, between Adnan and Isma'il, we do not know how many. And Isma'il is the son of Ibrahim. Between Ibrahim and Nuh, some reports mention 10, but in reality these do not go back to the Prophet ﷺ, and we do not have to believe in them. And also between Nuh and Adam, some reports again mention 10, but these are not a hadith. This is like people of the past, maybe even a companion, speaking. And so this is not something that we have to necessarily believe in, and we do not know, therefore, how many generations existed.

And in fact, it doesn't make sense for Allah to use the term *kathira*. Allah is saying lots of generations between them. And this is in the Qur'an, Surah Furqan, verse 38. And if you look at these charts, you find that there's only 10 people between Ibrahim and Nuh, and Nuh and Adam. Just 10 is not *kathir*, *kathira*. 10 is not that much that Allah is saying there were many generations between them. For Allah to say "many," it does not make sense that there's only 10.

And in fact, we have other evidences that might indicate this. Of them is the fact that Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala sent 124,000 prophets. 124,000 prophets; we know this from the ahadith. Now, the names of these prophets and their stories, even from common knowledge of history, we don't know. From our Qur'an and Sunnah we know around 25, and we can add another 20 or so names we're not certain about from the Old Testament. Because the Old Testament mentions some of the prophets that were between Sulayman, between Musa and between Isa. The Old Testament mentions all of the names of the prophets, so we can say, okay, this is what they know, and it's not something we need to accept or to reject. But still, the grand total that we would be able to get is less than, let's say, 50 names, and that's from including sources that are dubious, because the Judeo-Christian sources, we don't have to believe in them, but we can narrate them. So 120,000 prophets, and we do not even have knowledge of the majority of them.

The only way to explain this would be to extrapolate the beginning of mankind to many, many, many thousands of years ago, and then to posit that there were prophets that came in antiquity. There was no record, there was no writing, because again, reading and writing is something that was invented very, very recently. Allah blessed mankind with that. Otherwise, for most of human history, writing did not exist, and even paintings were rare. But they were there; they could draw. But the concept of writing, and speech being written down and recorded in alphabets or hieroglyphics, this is something that is relatively very, very, very recent in human history. It only goes back... we actually have records maybe 2,000, 3,000 at the very most. So in reality, we don't have... And of course, even those... by the way, hieroglyphics is not the type of writing that we do; it's basically symbol writing. So the point being that one of the ways to interpret and explain this would be to extrapolate the timeframe.

And another hadith that might indicate that the times are much beyond what we can comprehend is the famous hadith in Musnad Imam Ahmad (and its basis is also in Bukhari and others, and this version is in multiple books) that when Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala created the creation, when Allah created Adam, He extracted from Adam all of the souls, and He showed Adam all of these souls in front of him. And Adam saw the brightness: some were brighter than others and some were darker. This is the nur of iman. So Adam was particularly drawn to one particular light. And Adam said, "Who is this, O Allah? Who is this, that I can see a brightness coming from his forehead?" And Allah 'Azza wa Jall says, "This is one of the last of the generations of your descendants, by the name of Dawud. This is a man from the very last of your generations, by the name of Dawud."

And then the hadith goes on that Adam gifted Dawud 40 years of his own life. So Adam was initially destined to live a thousand years, and he gifted 40 to his son Dawud. So when the angel of death came at 960 years, Adam had forgotten that he had given 40, and he denied it, and Allah gifted him another 40. But the point is that he had gifted 40 to Dawud alayhi salam.

Now the point being, the interesting phrase that we have over here is that Allah 'Azza wa Jall says to Adam, "This is Dawud, who shall come in the very end of times." Now for us, we think of Dawud as living in ancient times. From our perspective, Dawud is the very beginnings of humanity. I mean, I'm stretching a little bit, but you get my point here. We think Dawud is a long, long time ago, even though of course technically he might have been 2,000 years from now; 1,000-something BC, 900-something BC is Dawud. So from our timeframe... sorry, 3,000 years from now, 3,000 years in the past. So from our timeframe, Dawud is 3,000 years ago, and that's way back.

And in the hadith we are told that Dawud is going to be at the very end of times, which indicates that from Adam to Dawud is such a large timeframe that Dawud is considered to be... Now, if it was 50,000 years, and Dawud is 3,000 years ago, then we understand: 50,000 years, and in the last 5,000 years. Allah knows when is the Day of Judgment. We ask Allah to not have us alive when that happens; we don't want to be there towards akhir al-zaman. But things are happening, and Allah knows how much time is left. We are living closer and closer to akhir al-zaman.

So the point being, once again (I hope you get what I'm saying here), if Dawud is akhir al-zaman and akhir al-umam, then where are we? And it does indicate that between Adam and Dawud is a far larger gap than a mere 2,000 that the Jewish calendar would have posited. Because the Jewish calendar would say there's around 2,000 between Adam and Dawud, and that means 4,000 between us and Dawud, or 3,000 between us and Dawud. So how then can Allah say that Dawud is the last of your ummahs, and he is in fact before even half of the 6,000? I hope you understand what I'm saying here.

So bottom line: **theologically, we have no obligation to believe in any number.** And in fact, I argue that the Qur'an and Sunnah might even indicate that 6,000 is too small of a number, and that in fact the notion of us having been here 50, 60,000 years actually makes more sense if you look at these other factors. And Allah says in the Qur'an that some of the prophets, We have told you their stories, and some We haven't. And so the majority of prophets are in such antiquity that we have no knowledge of them whatsoever. And therefore this explains this large gap, and Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala knows best.
